title: What a Town of Vibecoders Says About the Chinese Economy
title_cn: What a Town of Vibecoders Says About the Chinese Economy
summary: According to Stanford's AI Index, 84% of people surveyed in China say they are optimistic about AI. In the US, by contrast, 38% of those surveyed say they are optimistic. That's a big gulf in enthusiasm, and you can see it borne out in the stories you read: While in the US we hear about AI doomsday scenarios, in China, you'll hear about grandmas who are obsessed with using OpenClaw. Afra Wang has spent a lot of time in mainland China reporting from the country's AI hotbed — in a vibecoding-obsessed town outside of Hangzhou; at the for-profit schools where influencers are teaching everyday people how to use the technology; and the content studios that are pumping out AI microdramas. She understands, better than most, how AI is reshaping everyday life in China, and for today's episode, we talk to her about her reporting on AI in China and how the technology is actually diffusing into Chinese society.  (Source: Bloomberg)
